metadata.title: Kevin Coleman - No targets in loss
metadata.description: Coleman played 27 offensive snaps and saw no targets in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
metadata.analysis: Coleman played 46 percent of the Dolphins' offensive snaps in the blowout loss. The fifth-round rookie appears to have taken a backseat to Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas (ankle) and Chris Bell. Coleman could see an uptick in usage in the team's Week 3 game against the Chiefs if Douglas cannot play due to his ankle injury.

metadata.title: Kevin Coleman - Held without catch in NFL debut
metadata.description: Coleman failed to bring in his two targets during Sunday's 27-13 loss to Las Vegas.
metadata.analysis: Malik Willis missed on both of his pass attempts to Coleman late in the fourth quarter. Coleman's 16 snaps on offense were fourth-most among Dolphins wide receivers, and the rookie fifth-rounder figures to operate in a rotational role on offense behind Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell. Coleman will look to record his first NFL catch in a Week 2 tilt against the 49ers on Sept. 20.

metadata.title: Kevin Coleman Jr. sees two targets in Week 1
metadata.description: Kevin Coleman Jr. failed to catch either of his two targets in the Dolphins' 27-13 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 1.
metadata.analysis: Coleman Jr. was one of many minimally involved in the Miami passing attack in the season opener, finishing only ahead of Will Kacmarek in targets. The wideout can be left off rosters in all formats until further notice ahead of a Week 2 contest against the San Francisco 49ers.

metadata.title: Kevin Coleman - Team's leading receiver in preseason loss
metadata.description: Coleman (undisclosed) caught two of five targets for 32 yards in Saturday's 26-3 preseason loss to the Giants.
metadata.analysis: Coleman had previously dealt with an undisclosed injury that caused him to miss some practice time, but the rookie fifth-round pick suited up Saturday and paced the team in targets and receiving yards. The Dolphins rested their starters and got an ugly passing performance out of the backups, as Coleman was the only player on the team to exceed 12 receiving yards in the game. Coleman seems to be running well behind rookie third-round pick Caleb Douglas, as well as the more experienced Malik Washington, Jalen Tolbert and Tutu Atwell. Fellow rookie WR Chris Bell (knee) could also factor into the mix whenever he's cleared for game action.

metadata.title: Kevin Coleman - Misses practice Friday
metadata.description: Coleman missed Friday's practice due to an undisclosed injury, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
metadata.analysis: The rookie sixth-round pick doesn't seem to have made much noise early on at training camp, while third-round pick Caleb Douglas reportedly was one of the standouts at Friday's session. There's still time for Coleman to make his case for a role this summer if the injury he's dealing with doesn't turn out to be serious.

metadata.title: Kevin Coleman Jr. Could be a Taxi-Squad Stash Option
metadata.description: Miami Dolphins wide receiver Kevin Coleman Jr. should get plenty of opportunities to prove himself on this rebuilding roster. The Dolphins selected Coleman in the fifth-round of this year's draft. He was the third wideout taken by the Dolphins behind Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell. Despite being taken late in the draft, Coleman could quickly climb up the depth chart, assuming he plays well. He finished with 66 receptions, 732 receiving yards, and one touchdown across 13 games with Missouri this past season. Coleman did tear his ACL in November, which could impact his availability for the beginning of the season. Once he's healthy, Coleman should get a chance to prove himself on a roster without a ton of reliable pass-catchers. Coleman is unlikely to be a consistent contributor right away, but could have value down the road in dynasty formats. He's someone to think about stashing on the taxi squad.

metadata.title: Kevin Coleman Jr. in the Right Place for Opportunities
metadata.description: Wide receiver Kevin Coleman Jr. (knee) was the Miami Dolphins' third pass-catcher picked in this year's NFL draft, and although he has plenty to prove in a rebuilding organization, he certainly landed in one of the most wide-open WR corps in the NFL. The 22-year-old tore his ACL last November and isn't a lock to be ready for the start of his first year in the NFL this fall, putting him off the radar entirely in 2026 redraft fantasy leagues. In three collegiate seasons at Louisville, Mississippi State, and Missouri, he caught 166 passes for 2,206 yards and nine total touchdowns in 39 games played as primarily a slot receiver at 5-foot-10, 179 pounds. Coleman's injury and subpar 40-yard dash (4.49 seconds) dropped him all the way to the sixth round (177th overall), behind both fellow rookies Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell. There is plenty of opportunity in Miami, with Jalen Tolbert, Tutu Atwell, and Malik Washington currently serving as the team's top-three wideouts. Durability will be a concern for Coleman, but if he can stay on the field, he could challenge Washington for playing time sooner rather than later in South Beach. RotoBaller has Coleman ranked as the No. 108 WR in dynasty/keeper formats for the upcoming campaign.

metadata.title: Kevin Coleman - Scooped up by Miami
metadata.description: The Dolphins selected Coleman in the fifth round of the 2026 NFL Draft, 177th overall.
metadata.analysis: Coleman played for four different schools during his four-year college career, which ended in 2025 with Missouri, when he posted 66 catches for 732 yards and one touchdown across 13 games. He served primarily as a slot wide receiver and had the explosiveness to beat the first man, and his experience as a punt returner could earn him playing time in his rookie season in the NFL. Coleman is the third wide receiver selected by the Dolphins in this year's draft, joining Texas Tech's Caleb Douglas and Louisville's Chris Bell.

metadata.title: Kevin Coleman Jr. selected No. 177 by Miami Dolphins
metadata.description: The Miami Dolphins have selected WR Kevin Coleman Jr. with the No. 177 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
metadata.analysis: Coleman Jr. had a productive collegiate career, finishing with a 66-catch season at Missouri in 2025. He has good speed, but not top-end elite speed and his lack of size (5-10, 179) projects him to operate out of the slot in the NFL. However, he has excellent hands and can make defenders miss in the open field. The Dolphins have had a massive overhaul in their wide receiver room this offseason, so Coleman adds another player in the rotation heading into 2026.
